exposure: package of interventions (including capacity building for service providers)
outcome: obstetric outcomes (preterm labour, low birth weight, mode of delivery)
cohort: The study included 94 HIV-positive pregnant women (median age 32 years) in Oman, experiencing a total of 110 pregnancies between January 2016 and December 2019.
finding: The study found favorable obstetric and virological outcomes for HIV-infected pregnant women with 95.5% antiretroviral coverage, resulting in a low 1% rate of mother-to-child HIV transmission.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was the most common mode of delivery, accounting for 50% of births.
